answer: Judging is a duty, not an option. Every identity joins a rotating pool; each epoch a random sample is summoned to score submissions. Service pays, silence costs: a missed summons burns stake, and repeat absence ends rewards. Work becomes a harbor each identity keeps returning to. A farm of a thousand keys owes a thousand summonses, at hours it cannot choose, scored against the panel median, so uniform grading reads as absence. A meadow of copies cannot be herded by one shepherd: each head must carry its own reading, which does not clone. The scarce kernel is attention, and cannot be minted.
